questoes.enunciado: Identify the space around the tips of the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. During follicular development, following the primary multilaminar stage (late primary follicle), spaces begin to appear between the follicle cells. The spaces eventually coalesce into a single antral space or antrum. The presence of an antrum or antral spaces defines a secondary or antral follicle.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the organ that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: The mucosa of the vagina is composed of a stratified squamous moist epithelium and a well-vascularized lamina propria. No glands are present. Cells of the vaginal epithelium accumulate glycogen, indicated by their abundant, clear cytoplasm. The glycogen in sloughed cells is metabolized by resident bacteria to organic acids that maintain an acidic environment required for sperm capacitation. The acidity also discourages the growth of pathogenic bacteria.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures indicated by the rectangles.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. These follicles consist of a single row of flattened, follicular epithelial cells surrounding the primary oocyte. These are the only follicles present at birth and up until puberty, at which time cohorts primordial follicles begin further development with each successive ovarian cycle.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. All developing follicles, except the Graafian follicle, contain primary oocytes. They are arrested in prophase of meiosis 1. Just prior to ovulation, the first meiotic division is completed, resulting in the formation of a secondary oocyte and the first polar body. The secondary oocyte, which arrests in metaphase, is haploid and is released from the ovary at ovulation. Completion of meiosis occurs upon fertilization.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The zona pellucida, a highly refractile layer surrounding the oocyte plasma membrane, is composed of glycoproteins secreted by the oocyte and to some extent by the follicular cells immediately surrounding it. The zona pellucida is first evident at the primary, unilaminar follicle (early primary follicle) stage.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the double arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. A primary, multilaminar follicle (late primary follicle) forms as the follicle cells of a primary, unilaminar follicle proliferate to form a stratified epithelium. When antral spaces begin to appear between these cells, the follicle is then referred to as a secondary follicle. Antral spaces eventually fuse into a single space called the antrum.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the double arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Follicle cells surround and support the oocyte. In a secondary follicle these cells collectively form the stratum granulosum. They are responsive to follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) and secrete estrogen.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure outlined in this image.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The cumulus oophorus is a specialized region of the stratum granulosum in a secondary follicle. The cumulus surrounds the oocyte as it projects into the antral space. The subset of cumulus cells that immediately surround the oocyte is called the corona radiate and are released with oocyte at ovulation.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. A secondary follicle is defined as a follicle which contains antral spaces. Here, all of the original antral spaces have fused into one large cavity which is filled with follicular fluid. This space is the antrum.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the layer of cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The stratum granulosum is a stratified epithelium of follicle cells that lines the antral space.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the double arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The corpus albicans is the scar tissue remains of the corpus luteum. It has a shape similar to the corpus luteum, but since it is composed of scar tissue, it contains very few cells, mostly inactive fibroblasts. In contrast, the corpus luteum is highly cellular, filled with large, vacuolated, secretory cells.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the organ that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. During the secretory phase of the menstrual cycle, the uterine endometrium attains its greatest thickness and contains large, dilated glands and prominent spiral arteries. These changes are the result of progesterone and estrogen secretion from the corpus luteum. In addition the cells of the stroma, called pre-decidual cells, accumulate glycogen that serves as an early nutrient source for the embryo during implantation.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Spiral arteries are "cork-screw" shaped vessels that emerge at the junction of the basal and functional layers of the endometrium and extend into the functional layer. Because of their spiral configuration, spiral arteries appear as clusters of isolated, tubular profiles when sectioned longtitudinally.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the organ subdivision that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The cervix is the lower, cylindrical portion of the uterus and contains the endocervical canal. The lower part of the cervix extends into the vagina as the ectocervix. The abrupt junction of the simple columnar epithelium of the endocervical canal with the stratified squamous moist epithelium of the vaginal portion of the cervix is the external os. The endocervical canal is lined by a simple columnar epithelium with mucus-secreting glands or folds called plica palmatae.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the double arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Plicae palmatae are secretory folds of the cervical epithelium that secrete mucus. The quantity and consistency of the mucus changes during the menstrual cycle under the influence of the ovarian hormones.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the organ that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The ampulla of the oviduct (seen here) is characterized by numerous, branching folds of the mucosa. The lining epithelium is highly ciliated to propel the oocyte and also contains peg cells, whose secretory product nourishes the oocyte.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the organ that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. During the proliferative phase of the menstrual cycle, the stratum basale regenerates the stratum functionalis. The proliferative phase displays a relatively thin endometrium with straight glands that do not contain secretory material. The spiral arteries are not coiled nor readily visible.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. These simple tubular glands extend through the endometrium. During the proliferative phase of the menstrual cycle, as shown here, the glands are straight and do not contain secretory material. In response to progesterone during the luteal phase of the ovarian cycle, these glands enlarge, accumulate secretory material and appear sacculated with “saw-tooth” lumens.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the layer indicated by the double arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. In this section of the proliferative uterus, the entire endometrium, with both the functional zone and the basal zone, are visible. Estrogen from ovarian follicles supports this stage.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the organ that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. During pregnancy, the tubular duct elements of the mammary glands elongate and branch, and alveoli begin to develop from the ducts. Some secretory product may be present in the alveoli and the ducts, particularly during the third trimester of pregnancy. At this stage, the amount of parenchymal and stromal components appear about equal.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Intralobular ducts are surrounded by the secretory parenchyma of the mammary gland and lie completely within the mammary gland lobule. These ducts eventually join others to form interlobular ducts that are surrounded by connective tissue in the interlobular stroma.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The chorionic plate is composed of fetal tissue and is located outside the amnion surrounding the fetus. It is composed of fetal connective tissue covered by trophoblast. Fetal blood vessels penetrate the chorionic plate to enter the chorionic villi.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the layer indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The syncytiotrophoblast surrounds each chorionic villus like a rind. It faces the intervillous spaces which is filled with maternal blood. The syncytiotrophoblast is formed from cytotrophoblasti cells and represents a single cell as the individual cell membrane fuse. The syncytiotrophoblast is the source of the placental hormones, estrogen, progesterone, human chorionic gonadotropin and placental lactogen.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Two types of villi originate from the chorionic plate, stem and anchoring villi. Stem villi extend into the intervillous space and support numerous, branching villi, termed floating villi. Anchoring villi extend to the maternal side of the placenta, anchoring the chorionic plate to the trophoblastic shell and, indirectly, to the decidua. Embryonic connective tissue does not extend the entire length of anchoring villi and thus their distal ends contain a core of cytotrophoblast cells.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the organ that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: Correct. The menstrual phase of the uterus follows the ischemic phase and is marked by the sloughing of the functional layer of the endometrium, including the surface epithelium and most of the uterine glands. These tissues constitute the menstrual flow or menses. The basal layer of the endometrium remains, which regenerates the functional layer during the proliferative phase.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the organ that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This initial period of the menstrual phase is referred to as the ischemic phase which results from the alternate contraction and relaxation of the spiral arteries. This result in the extravasation (bleeding) of red blood cells, tissue necrosis and loosening of the functional layer of the endometrium. The surface epithelium is still intact.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the layer indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The theca interna contains secretory cells that possess cytological features characteristic of steroid-producing cells, most obvious being the presence of large lipid droplets in the cytoplasm. The theca interna is also highly vascularized. The theca externa, beyond this layer, appears more like connective tissue. Cells of the theca interna synthesize and secrete androgen which is converted to estrogen by the granulosa cells.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure shown in this image.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The external os demonstrates the abrupt junction of the simple columnar epithelium lining the endocervical canal (above) with the stratified squamous moist epithelium that covers the ectocervix (below). The stratified epithelium covers the remainder of the ectocervix and is reflected onto the inner surface of the vagina.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the organ that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. After ovulation, the follicle wall collapses resulting in the deeply folded structure of the corpus luteum. During the formation of the corpus luteum, cells of both the granulosa and theca interna of the Graafian follicle differentiate forming granulosa lutein and theca lutein cells, respectively. This process is called luteinization. Both populations of luteal cells secrete progesterone and estrogens.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the organ that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The lactation stage of the breast is marked by the presence of large, milk-filled, and widely distended alveoli. Milk production is not synchronous among all the lobules, as seen here, or even within a single lobule. At this stage, the parenchyma of the organ is predominant. This abundant milk production is regulated by prolactin secreted from the anterior pituitary.
